lines.text: Almost every Austrian is an organ donor. In Germany, only about twelve percent are.
lines.headline: ==99.98%== vs *12%*

lines.text: Two neighbours, with similar culture, wealth and values.
lines.headline: Same *neighbours*

lines.text: In 2003, Eric Johnson and Daniel Goldstein showed the gap came down to one checkbox.
lines.headline: Johnson & Goldstein, *2003*

lines.text: In Austria, you're a donor unless you opt out.
lines.headline: Opt *out*

lines.text: In Germany, you have to tick the box to opt in.
lines.headline: Opt *in*

lines.text: Across Europe, opt-out countries sat near the top. Opt-in countries, far below.
lines.headline: The *default* wins

lines.text: But nobody was forced. Doing nothing is easy, and a ticked box feels like advice.
lines.headline: Nobody was *forced*

lines.text: Check your settings, subscriptions and auto-renewals today. And follow for more choices that were never really yours.
lines.headline: Check your *defaults*

post.title: Why Austria Has 99.98% Organ Donors and Germany 12% #shorts
post.description: Johnson & Goldstein (2003, Science, 'Do Defaults Save Lives?'): in opt-out Austria 99.98% were organ donors vs about 12% in opt-in Germany. Nobody was forced; people kept whatever was pre-selected. The default effect. #psychology #shorts #defaulteffect #nudge
